personas.label: Plant-biology researcher checking what is established
personas.situation: Works on one perception pathway (for example wound signalling or light) and uses the app to see what is established, what is proposed or contested, and what is still a gap, before writing or planning experiments.
personas.deciding: Which steps are safe to cite, which are proposed or single-study, and where the gaps are.
jobs: See every gap and every flag on a path before I cite it
Tell an established receptor from a proposed mechanism or a single-study claim
Check which senses really share a receptor, without being misled by study volume
Sketch a hypothesis linking two pathways and see which links have curated support

personas.label: Graduate student learning a plant pathway end to end
personas.situation: New to one branch (for example photoreceptors or immunity); follows a sense from stimulus to response and looks at the molecules in 3D.
personas.deciding: What to read first, and which structure to look at for a journal club or a figure.
jobs: Follow one sense from stimulus to response and know what is not yet supported
Open a receptor, see its structure, and tell experimental from predicted and whole protein from domain
See the chromophore or hormone a receptor binds

personas.label: Educator preparing teaching material on how plants sense
personas.situation: Builds a lecture or lab on plant perception for undergraduates; needs a trustworthy overview, clear labels for contested claims and for evidence from other species, and figures to export.
personas.deciding: Which pathways to teach as established, how to present contested claims, and which visuals to use.
jobs: Show the range of plant senses on one tree, including the contested ones, clearly labelled
Find which rows come from species other than Arabidopsis
Export a filtered evidence table and a navigator figure
